data.current_description:
The paired report as scored right now: per arm, per pair, each comparison against the control, the decision and a verdict.

The same report the Studio's experiment panel shows. experiment.arms lists each arm with what it changes against the control (differs_from_control, paths of the arm's request), its trial counts, its score over the scored trials (mean, interquartile mean, median, spread, a 95% Student t interval over the arm's trials), cost, usage (spend per finished trial, spend per index point, and per model the tokens and spend per seat per trial over its scored trials, in that model's own tokens; guest seats are counted as unmeasured_seats and enter no figure), and the awareness split (how many seats said they were being evaluated and how they scored against the seats that said the match was real). An experiment that declares output per turn, as its metric or a secondary outcome, gives each arm effort: per model the mean output tokens per play turn over its measured seats, thinking tokens per turn alone (null when the route itemized none), the share of play turns cut off at the seat's output cap, and which upstream hosts served its calls, with how many seats were measured, how many missed more than a tenth of their rounds (short_seats) and how many had nothing to read (unmeasured_seats: a guest, or no output reported); each figure is in that model's own tokens and compares only with the same model. Output per turn analyzes on the log scale: an arm's per-trial value is the geometric mean over the seats measured in every arm that trial, so a difference is the mean of each model's log ratio against itself, and its detail prints it as a percent change. experiment.pairs is every trial index with the per-arm value and its seeds; a trial index is excluded and says why when any arm's trial there failed, was cancelled, lost a seat to an error, was stopped short of its season by the spend cap, was picked up by a new server release mid-match (its resumes: from that round its seats played without their memory of the earlier rounds, a condition the other arm did not play) or has not finished, because a half-played match never enters a pair; an arm whose comparison already stopped is not needed after its last pair, and the control only while some comparison still is, so a trial missing there excludes nothing. experiment.comparisons is each arm against the control: paired trials seen (n) and the last trial index among them (last_trial), the mean difference on the analysis scale, the rule's stop, reason and verdict (arm_better, control_better, undecided, or null when the rule has not looked or had fewer than 3 pairs to look at; output per turn and the debrief share, which have no better side, read arm_higher or control_higher) with its interval, and a comparison that stopped keeps the numbers of its stop; a finished experiment the rule never stopped (a trial failed or could not be scored, so fewer pairs than trials) gets the rule's last look on the pairs present, and its detail says how many trial indexes produced no pair. exact is the fixed rule's exact two-sided sign-flip test at its look, beside the t test the rule reads: unit pair, or world when worlds repeat (each world's pairs flip together), how many units, the p, and min_p, the smallest p so few units allow whatever the effect (0.0625 at five, which no exact test can bring under 0.05). It decides nothing, and is null under the anytime rule (which looks again and again, so a test read at its stop holds no level), before the look, and past 20 units. by_world is null when every pair played a world of its own; when the pairs replayed worlds (a seed pool of fewer maps than trials, or one pinned map) it gives how many world seeds the pairs played (worlds), how many more than once (repeated), and the cluster-robust Student t interval that counts each world once (CR1, on worlds minus one degrees of freedom, at the comparison's level), which is what carries to worlds drawn the same way: the rule's own interval counts pairs and holds for the worlds played. That interval is null under the anytime rule, below three worlds, and when the worlds came out alike. reason is owner for a comparison the owner stopped (the experiment cancelled, or its arm dropped in the Studio): under the anytime rule past its first look it keeps the sequence's interval and verdict at that stop, which holds at any stopping time; under the fixed rule, or before the first look, its verdict is null, since a single look read early at a time the owner chose holds no level. The verdict sentence names how many trials each arm lost when the losses fall unevenly. experiment.secondary is each outcome declared beside the metric, in the order declared: its per-trial values and, per arm against the control, the paired difference read on the same pairs with the same rule at the same level, its interval, a reading in the verdict's words, and its own exact and by_world; a reading decides nothing, and once a comparison stops its secondaries are read on the pairs it stopped on. Each secondary interval holds its level on its own, not jointly with the metric's. detectable_gap is the smallest true gap the design finds with 80% power, on Student t, from the observed spread once five pairs are in and the prior before that; its by_world, when the trials replay worlds, gives how many and the most a reading that counts each world once can need (null under the anytime rule and below three worlds). decision is the rule's standing and summary the rule in words; verdict is plain language that leads with what the numbers do not yet support. note is your note (your declared result, in your words, with note_at_ms when you last wrote it) and design the design document's digest, size, arrival and standing, both as the list shows them. runs carries every trial's run record, one array per arm. Your own experiments only; another account's reads as unknown.

data.current_description:
Every world your account has playing right now, as small boards, and every run waiting for one.

What the Studio's Live page draws, in one read for all of them. Each world carries its round and length, how long the current round has waited (round_age_ms), the terrain as one letter per cell row by row (f forest, m mountain, p plains, w water, r ruins; it does not change during a match), each agent's cell, status and color (its creature's palette, 0 to 7, as the Live world page paints it; roster seats first, then the scenario's baseline bots), the top three, spend against the run's cap, flags and heads_up. A flag is something only you can fix while fixing it still changes how the world plays, and it names the one thing to do: action is that instruction and action_url where to do it (a provider page, or null). Its code is out_of_credit (the provider refused a seat on your own key for lack of credit; credit added now reaches the seat's next try, and a seat stops after 5 failed model calls in a row) or guest_quiet (a guest seat stopped calling in and the world no longer waits for it; its guest can come back). A heads-up is worth knowing with nothing to do: model_errors or rate_limited (a seat's last two or more model calls failed in a row, counted the way the harness counts them, with no call landing between; one failed call is routine and shows nothing, and a refused key shows from the first), seat_stopped (the seat stopped playing and the world plays on without it), forfeiting (three or more turns missed in a row), spend_near_cap (80% of the cap) and time_near_cap (less than a tenth of the time cap left). seat names the seat, or is null on the last two, which are about the run as a whole; text is the sentence the Live page shows. last_event is the latest public action. Direct messages, notes, key events and reasoning never appear. A world in a series or an experiment names its study in group (trial counts from 0, like the run record's batch.trial). waiting lists your runs still waiting for a world, each with starts_in_ms, when it is expected to start (an estimate from the pace of the worlds ahead of it, or their time caps; null while guest seats are out): in_line with the place in line across the platform, own_limit when your plan's runs at once are all playing (it starts as one of your runs ends), guests while guest seats are out. totals counts the worlds playing, the runs waiting and needs_you (worlds carrying at least one flag; heads-ups never count), with spend_usd summed over the playing worlds and caps_usd the sum of their caps. Open a world full size at watch_url while signed in to the Studio. Your own runs only.

data.current_description:
A series batch as one report: per-model intervals, survival, cost, every trial, and a verdict.

The same report the Studio's batch panel shows. batch.models folds every scored trial into one row per model: a 95% Student t interval on the mean over trials, each trial counted once however many seats the model held in it, and kept within the index's 0 to 100 (the headline; null below two trials), the mean with the interquartile mean beside it (a gap between them is the tail), the median, spread, best and worst, survival as a rate with its interval, wins, and provisional while the model has fewer than three scored trials, and usage: what the model's seats consumed per seat per trial (tokens_in_mean, tokens_out_mean, spend_usd_mean), the total, and spend per index point and per win, all over the seats the platform metered (measured_seats; unmeasured_seats counts the rest, a guest seat on its own keys, which enter none of these figures). Tokens are counted by each model's own tokenizer, so they compare a model with itself; compare models on spend. spend_usd is the provider's own charge where the route reports one, else priced from the published table; approximate is true when some call was priced that way at a fallback rate because the table lists no price for its model. batch.points lists every trial with its seeds, its awareness frame and its per-seat outcome, each seat with its usage (calls, tokens_in with its cache_read_tokens, tokens_out with its reasoning_tokens, spend_usd, approximate, and on seats metered since output per turn became an outcome the play turns alone as turn_calls, turn_tokens_out, turn_reasoning_tokens and turn_truncated, with turn_skipped, the rounds a dormant seat sat out with no model call, on seats metered since harness 0.6.5; null when not measured, never zero), null until that trial has a scoreable archive. batch.cost sums the trials' meters so far. batch.verdict is a plain-language reading that leads with what the batch does not yet support. runs carries every trial's run record; arena is the scoreline when the batch is an arena series, null otherwise. Your own batches only; a batch on another account reads as unknown.

data.current_description:
What creating this experiment would cost and check against, or the refusal it would get. Nothing is queued.

The same validation and receipts as a creation: the arms, one scenario, no seed of an arm's own, the trial count against the plan, the rule, one queue slot per arm against the plan and against what is free now, then each arm through the launch admission (plan ceilings, seat funding, quota). arms carries each arm's estimate exactly as POST /runs/estimate answers for a batch of trials. design is the whole experiment: the cost summed over the arms, the wall clock of the longest arm (arms run side by side), the queue slots it holds, the rule as locked, and detectable_gap, the smallest true gap this design finds with 80% power by its cap, on Student t at the cap's degrees of freedom, from the prior per-seat spread at the arms' season length (null on a metric the prior was not measured on). For output per turn the prior is the per-model spread of a four-model pilot and the gap is in log units: 0.05 is a change of about 5%. detectable_gap.by_world is null when every trial plays a map of its own; when the trials replay maps (a scenario whose seed pool holds fewer maps than the trials, or one pinned map) it gives how many maps (worlds) and the most a reading that counts each map once, which is what carries to other maps, can need (gap), reached when the effect differs wholly from map to map; that gap is null under the anytime rule, which prints no such reading, and below three maps. detectable_gap.at_trials lists the same gap at 10, 20 and 30 trials per arm, those above the design's own and within the plan, under the rule the design would take there (the chosen kind, or fixed to 10 and anytime above), so a builder can say what more trials would show; empty where gap is null. A study's re-run (replicates) estimates the design the server builds from the study, and rerun says which study it re-runs and whether it would play that study exactly as recorded (exact, with differences when not: a seat that carried its owner's private text, a scenario or scaffold that changed since, a different stopping rule); rerun is null on any other body. A body a creation would refuse answers with the creation's error code. Free tokens may call this.

data.current_description:
Queue a paired experiment: two to four arms of one scenario on shared seeds, under a stopping rule.

Answers 201 with the experiment as the list shows it. Each arm becomes a series batch of trials runs (arms[].batch_id), and trial i of every arm plays the same world seed and the same spawn seed, so the per-trial difference between an arm and the control is what the arms differ in. Arms run side by side, one of your plan's runs at once each, and each trial is named <experiment> · <arm>. The stopping rule is locked here and is the only thing that looks at the result: the experiment ends when the rule decides, when the whole interval lies within plus or minus target_half_width, or when every trial has played; a rule stop cancels the trials still to play under the rule's reason, not yours. With three or four arms each comparison against the control stops on its own and keeps the verdict and interval of its stop: its arm's trials still to play are cancelled while the control and the other arms play on, and the experiment ends once every comparison has stopped. It is recorded finished only once every trial has ended. Inference bills to your own keys on every arm. A body of replicates (a published study's experiment id) queues that study again whole on your keys, published from creation; its record carries replicates. Estimate first. Needs a paid plan.

data.current_description:
What a launch of this body would cost and commit, or the refusal it would get. Nothing is queued.

The same validation and receipts as a launch: plan ceilings, who funds each seat, the agent-turn reservation, the USD and wall-clock range, quota and queue headroom, and how much precision the trial count buys. funding has one entry per roster seat, in order: user (billed to your keys), sponsored (the platform pays, where offered) or guest (an invited seat, played on the guest's own keys and left out of the reservation and the cost range). A body a launch would refuse answers with the launch's error code. Free tokens may call this.

The top-level cost fields (usdLow, usdHigh, agentTurns, minutesLow, minutesHigh) are ONE trial; batch is the same figures for every trial you asked for, which is what the launch actually commits. hitsRunCap says the plan's run-time cap is what ended the wall-clock range, not the scenario.

perSeat[].source says where each seat's price came from: catalog is the provider's own published rate, table a tier in Daishi's price table, and fallback a pattern standing in for a model nobody has priced yet. approximate is true when any seat is fallback, and it means the whole band is a guess — the spend cap is still enforced against it, so a model priced above its vendor's cheapest tier can pass a cap it would really have crossed.

data.current_description:
One log file, as the JSONL the harness wrote.

Answers application/x-ndjson with the file verbatim, one JSON object per line, in the order it was written. **The example below is one line of a trajectory file, not the whole body** — not re-encoded, because a trajectory is evidence and a reader should be able to verify the bytes that were recorded. Every trajectory line carries at (when it was written, ISO 8601) and type. A trajectory file opens with a header line (the seat name, its scaffold identity and the harness version), then holds one turn line per model call: tick, the observation the seat was sent, model_text and any model_reasoning, the tool_call it made, the action and args that ran, ok, result_summary, usage and latency_ms; exit_interview, awareness_probe, model_error and budget_stop lines appear as they happen, and a summary line closes the file. The other fields vary by line type. A usage file line has no type: it carries at, tick and kind (the call it records: turn, epilogue or probe), the model and the token counts under gen_ai.-prefixed keys (gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens, gen_ai.usage.output_tokens and the rest), and, unprefixed beside them, latency_ms and cost_usd (when the provider reported a cost). Name the file exactly as the list endpoint returned it. A trajectory holds the instructions you attached to the seat verbatim, so this is your own runs only, never cached by an intermediary and never public.
data.summary_suggestion: Retrieve a run's trajectory or usage log file

Supports two file types: trajectory files (containing seat instructions, model calls, observations, tool calls, and execution details per turn) and usage files (containing token counts, latency, and cost metrics). Returns the raw bytes as recorded by the harness without re-encoding to preserve evidence integrity. Requires authentication and access to your own runs only. File names must match exactly as returned by the seats endpoint.

data.current_description:
The paired report as scored right now: per arm, per pair, each comparison against the control, the decision and a verdict.

The same report the Studio's experiment panel shows. experiment.arms lists each arm with what it changes against the control (differs_from_control, paths of the arm's request), its trial counts, its score over the scored trials (mean, interquartile mean, median, spread, a 95% Student t interval over the arm's trials), cost, usage (spend per finished trial, spend per index point, and per model the tokens and spend per seat per trial over its scored trials, in that model's own tokens; guest seats are counted as unmeasured_seats and enter no figure), and the awareness split (how many seats said they were being evaluated and how they scored against the seats that said the match was real). An experiment that declares output per turn, as its metric or a secondary outcome, gives each arm effort: per model the mean output tokens per play turn over its measured seats, thinking tokens per turn alone (null when the route itemized none), the share of play turns cut off at the seat's output cap, and which upstream hosts served its calls, with how many seats were measured, how many missed more than a tenth of their rounds (short_seats) and how many had nothing to read (unmeasured_seats: a guest, or no output reported); each figure is in that model's own tokens and compares only with the same model. Output per turn analyzes on the log scale: an arm's per-trial value is the geometric mean over the seats measured in every arm that trial, so a difference is the mean of each model's log ratio against itself, and its detail prints it as a percent change. experiment.pairs is every trial index with the per-arm value and its seeds; a trial index is excluded and says why when any arm's trial there failed, was cancelled, lost a seat to an error, was stopped short of its season by the spend cap, was picked up by a new server release mid-match (its resumes: from that round its seats played without their memory of the earlier rounds, a condition the other arm did not play) or has not finished, because a half-played match never enters a pair; an arm whose comparison already stopped is not needed after its last pair, and the control only while some comparison still is, so a trial missing there excludes nothing. experiment.comparisons is each arm against the control: paired trials seen (n) and the last trial index among them (last_trial), the mean difference on the analysis scale, the rule's stop, reason and verdict (arm_better, control_better, undecided, or null when the rule has not looked or had fewer than 3 pairs to look at; output per turn and the debrief share, which have no better side, read arm_higher or control_higher) with its interval, and a comparison that stopped keeps the numbers of its stop; a finished experiment the rule never stopped (a trial failed or could not be scored, so fewer pairs than trials) gets the rule's last look on the pairs present, and its detail says how many trial indexes produced no pair. exact is the fixed rule's exact two-sided sign-flip test at its look, beside the t test the rule reads: unit pair, or world when worlds repeat (each world's pairs flip together), how many units, the p, and min_p, the smallest p so few units allow whatever the effect (0.0625 at five, which no exact test can bring under 0.05). It decides nothing, and is null under the anytime rule (which looks again and again, so a test read at its stop holds no level), before the look, and past 20 units. by_world is null when every pair played a world of its own; when the pairs replayed worlds (a seed pool of fewer maps than trials, or one pinned map) it gives how many world seeds the pairs played (worlds), how many more than once (repeated), and the cluster-robust Student t interval that counts each world once (CR1, on worlds minus one degrees of freedom, at the comparison's level), which is what carries to worlds drawn the same way: the rule's own interval counts pairs and holds for the worlds played. That interval is null under the anytime rule, below three worlds, and when the worlds came out alike. reason is owner for a comparison the owner stopped (the experiment cancelled, or its arm dropped in the Studio): under the anytime rule past its first look it keeps the sequence's interval and verdict at that stop, which holds at any stopping time; under the fixed rule, or before the first look, its verdict is null, since a single look read early at a time the owner chose holds no level. The verdict sentence names how many trials each arm lost when the losses fall unevenly. experiment.secondary is each outcome declared beside the metric, in the order declared: its per-trial values and, per arm against the control, the paired difference read on the same pairs with the same rule at the same level, its interval, a reading in the verdict's words, and its own exact and by_world; a reading decides nothing, and once a comparison stops its secondaries are read on the pairs it stopped on. Each secondary interval holds its level on its own, not jointly with the metric's. detectable_gap is the smallest true gap the design finds with 80% power, on Student t, from the observed spread once five pairs are in and the prior before that; its by_world, when the trials replay worlds, gives how many and the most a reading that counts each world once can need (null under the anytime rule and below three worlds). decision is the rule's standing and summary the rule in words; verdict is plain language that leads with what the numbers do not yet support. note is your note (your declared result, in your words, with note_at_ms when you last wrote it) and design the design document's digest, size, arrival and standing, both as the list shows them. runs carries every trial's run record, one array per arm. Your own experiments only; another account's reads as unknown.

Every world your account has playing right now, as small boards, and every run waiting for one.

What the Studio's Live page draws, in one read for all of them. Each world carries its round and length, how long the current round has waited (round_age_ms), the terrain as one letter per cell row by row (f forest, m mountain, p plains, w water, r ruins; it does not change during a match), each agent's cell, status and color (its creature's palette, 0 to 7, as the Live world page paints it; roster seats first, then the scenario's baseline bots), the top three, spend against the run's cap, flags and heads_up. Arms run side by side, one of your plan's runs at once each, and each trial is named <experiment> · <arm>. The stopping rule is locked here and is the only thing that looks at the result: the experiment ends when the rule decides, when the whole interval lies within plus or minus target_half_width, or when every trial has played; a rule stop cancels the trials still to play under the rule's reason, not yours. With three or four arms each comparison against the control stops on its own and keeps the verdict and interval of its stop: its arm's trials still to play are cancelled while the control and the other arms play on, and the experiment ends once every comparison has stopped. It is recorded finished only once every trial has ended. Inference bills to your own keys on every arm. A body of replicates (a published study's experiment id) queues that study again whole on your keys, published from creation; its record carries replicates. Estimate first. Needs a paid plan.
